chapter: New Orleans scene and jazz club
title: Sitting in at the New Orleans Jazz Club
summary: How jamming works at the Jazz Club; Schiro stayed on his own and steady.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, he plays alright, but there's something like it. Some of it is. You know he drives a pony around? He's got a pony and a car and drives him around the channel. Yeah. That gets his kicks. I'm not done. Well, what happens at the New Orleans Jazz Club when you go up there to play? How does that work? I never have played there. I haven't played in years, so I don't know. I used to play a couple of games.

Well, sometimes the boys sort of, like Dutch Andrews and a few others, they sort of pick something in there and they ask you if you want to play. If they happen to hear the trumpet or the clarinet man, hey, they go in the audience stand. They make an announcement for a trumpet man or somebody and they form a group and off they go.
Just like that, just jamming, huh? Yeah, jamming.
I mean, any number that they all agree upon, I guess.
Do you ever get any jobs up there by meeting guys and stuff? Nothing.
No, I was always on my own most of the time.
Well, I guess you're always steady with some of them for years and years. I had a lot of offers and all, but I mean.
I didn't try to push myself, you know, too far. But probably he had a pen, man. I got it on my mind.
